newsitem.title: FRANCE: Swiss cargo highlights increased ex-Brussels cargo.
newsitem.headline: Swiss cargo highlights increased ex-Brussels cargo.

text.p: Swiss Cargo, the cargo arm of Swissair, said air freight forwarders would soon be able to take advantage of greater cargo lift from Brussels to French-speaking West Africa following a decision by the Belgian airline Sabena to change the type of aircraft on these routes.
In October 1996, Swissair announced it would be marketing Sabena' total cargo capacity, effective January 1 1997, as part of a global alliance with the Belgian airline.

Swiss Cargo, an independent business unit since the beginning of the year, recently outlined plans to develop Brussels as its cargo hub in northern Europe which will entail the launch of several full-freighter flights.
The hub will serve France, Scandinavia, the Benelux and Britain.

Sabena is to replace Airbus 310 passenger aircraft by Airbus 330s and 340s on services to West Africa with the introduction of summer 1997 schedules at the end of March. This will increase the number of pallet positions considerably and double freight capacity on these routes," Swiss Cargo's cargo director, Northern Europe/Africa, Didier Mauger, told Reuters.
Sabena's A310 destinations in West Africa include, Abidjan, Accra, Bamako, Banjul, Conakry, Cotonou, Dakar, Freetown, Lagos, Libreville, Lome, Nouakchott Ouagadougou, Port Gentil and Yaounde.
The Northern Europe hub project is being presented to Swissair cargo managers from around the world at a two-day "kick-off" conference in Brussels beginning this evening, Mauger said.

"We have ambitious plans for Brussels and could have around ten full-freighter flights operating from the airport by 2000. However, as an independent business unit, the onus is on us more than ever to see these plans through to realisation, he added. Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax 5017
